key: Therefore the sage, in the exercise of his government, empties their minds, fills their bellies, weakens their wills, and strengthens their bones.
s: After counsel to keep the people from rivalry and theft, the verse turns to the sage’s rule; the Heshang Gong commentary, on chapter 3, reads it as governing state and self alike, the mind cleared of cravings, the bones firmed by husbanding the vital essence.
src: The Heshang Gong commentary, Laozi Daodejing Heshang Gong zhangju, chapter 3, zh.wikisource (a normalised text), revision 2019760 (2021)

evidence.words: 說聖人治國與治身同也。 … 除嗜欲，去亂煩。 … 愛精重施，髓滿骨堅。
evidence.gloss: (On the sage’s governing:) this says the sage’s governing of the state is the same as his governing of the self. … (On emptying the mind:) he removes cravings and clears away confusion and vexation. … (On strengthening the bones:) he cherishes the vital essence and is sparing in spending it, so the marrow is full and the bones firm.
